neighbours.label: Fires on the set of possible outcomes in a probability or counting problem (outcomes of dice, slots of a roulette wheel, the space of equally likely cases); quiet on the same words and counting structures outside chance.
fire: If you flip three coins, list all of the outcomes and count those with two heads.
A standard deck has 52 cards, and thirteen of the cards are hearts.
To find the probability, divide the sample space into equally likely cases.
On a fair die each of the six faces has the same chance of landing up.
Of the 38 slots on the wheel, eighteen of the slots are red.
Count the favorable outcomes and divide by the total number of possible outcomes.
Each of the possible outcomes of the spinner is equally likely.
When two dice are thrown, the space of outcomes has 36 equally likely pairs.
quiet: If you visit three cities, list all of the museums and count those with free entry.
A large parking lot has 52 spaces, and thirteen of the spaces are covered.
To finish the attic, divide the storage space into two equal rooms.
On a cold day each of the six windows was covered in frost.
Of the 38 rooms in the hotel, eighteen of the rooms face the sea.
Count the guests at the door and write the total in the book.
Each of the outcomes of the peace talks was reported in the press.
When two trains collide, the outcomes can be tragic for passengers.

predictions: median fire ~0.4 (probes: dice 'outcomes' 0.82, roulette 0.61, space of possibilities 0.41); near misses < 0.1 ('outcomes of the meeting' 0.014, 'office space' 0.034); risk: 'eighteen of the rooms' counting frame.
notes: Top examples: 'dividing the space of possibilities', 'frequency of outcomes', roulette numbers.
